title: The real price of a loan
topic: The full price of a loan

steps.title: 5.9% or 7.5%?
steps.body: €8,000 over 24 months. Offer A: 5.9% a year, plus a €300 fee and €600 loan insurance added to the loan. Offer B: 7.5% a year, nothing else. A looks cheaper. With the fee and insurance, A costs about €9,460 in total, B about €8,640. In the EU, lenders must also show the APR: the interest and the fees as one yearly rate. It is the [[total-cost-of-credit]] in one number.

stat.label: more paid back with the “cheaper” 5.9% offer

steps.prompt: Match each part of a loan offer with what it is.
pairs: The price of the borrowed money, per year
A one-off charge to set up the loan
An extra paid in case you can't repay
Interest and fees together, as one yearly rate

steps.prompt: Offer A: 5.9% interest, APR about 18% with its fees. Offer B: 7.5% interest, APR 7.5%. Which costs you less?
steps.explanation: Compare the total cost, not the headline rate. B's 7.5% is all there is. A's fee and insurance push its real cost far higher.

steps.prompt: Why might a lender advertise a low rate and add fees on top?
options: The low rate catches the eye, while the fees raise the real cost
Fees make the loan safer for the borrower
steps.explanation: People compare the number they see first. Fees and add-ons are where [[hidden-interest]] lives.
